fund_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me compile financial statements needed for a 409A valuation. The data source is {{vendor}}, our accounting system, accessed via your configured credentials.

Before starting, ask me for: (1) the reporting period(s) required for the valuation (typically the most recent fiscal year-end plus current period, but confirm with me), and (2) whether the valuation firm wants cash or accrual basis reporting.

Once I confirm those details, please:
1. Connect to {{vendor}} and retrieve the Profit & Loss report for the specified period(s) using the documented reporting API.
2. Retrieve the Balance Sheet report for the same period(s) using the documented reporting API.
3. If accessible through the same API, also pull the general ledger and trial balance for the period(s), as valuation firms often request these for backup detail.
4. Export each report in an open, standard format (CSV or similar) and organize them clearly by statement type and period.
5. Do a basic sanity check: confirm the Balance Sheet balances (assets = liabilities + equity) and that the P&L period dates match what I specified.
6. Compile all statements into a single organized folder or document set, labeled clearly (e.g., "P&L - [period]", "Balance Sheet - [period]").

Done looks like: a complete, organized package of P&L, Balance Sheet, and (if available) general ledger/trial balance for the requested period(s), pulled directly from {{vendor}}, with basic accuracy checks passed and no missing periods.

Report back with: which statements you successfully retrieved, the periods covered, the format/location of the compiled files, results of your sanity checks, and any discrepancies, missing data, or API access issues you encountered. Flag anything that looks inconsistent so I can review before sending these to the valuation firm.

fund_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me gather a cap table snapshot in preparation for commissioning a 409A valuation. Our equity management platform is {{vendor}}. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} issuer/company identifier, (2) confirmation that you should use my configured credentials to access {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard, and (3) any specific as-of date the valuation firm wants the snapshot dated.

Using {{vendor}}'s programmatic API (or dashboard export if the API isn't available), please:
1. Retrieve the current capitalization table broken out by share class (common, preferred, SAFEs, option pools, etc.).
2. List all stakeholders on the cap table with their holdings.
3. Pull any fair market values on record from prior 409A valuations, if available, for reference/comparison.
4. Export the full transaction history and cap table to an open format (CSV/Excel) so the data isn't locked into a proprietary format.
5. Reconcile the exported snapshot against any existing data room cap table file I have on hand, flagging discrepancies in stakeholder counts, share totals, or grant dates.

Done looks like: a clean, exported cap table snapshot (CSV/Excel) covering share classes, stakeholders, SAFEs, and option grants with vesting states, dated as of the requested date, plus a short reconciliation note listing any mismatches found versus prior records, and a note of any prior 409A fair market values retrieved.

Report back with: the file(s) or data produced, a summary of total fully-diluted shares and stakeholder count, any discrepancies flagged during reconciliation, and confirmation of the snapshot date — so I can hand this package to the 409A valuation provider.

fund_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a 409A valuation order in {{vendor}}, our equity management platform, ahead of an authorized officer's sign-off. Do not submit or authorize the engagement yourself — this requires a human officer's approval.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: our {{vendor}} account login context (I will use my own configured credentials), our company legal name, entity type, most recent funding round details (date, price per share, amount raised), and the desired valuation date or refresh schedule (e.g., quarterly, or triggered by next round).

Actions to take:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials.
2. Navigate to the 409A valuation ordering/intake section.
3. Confirm our live cap table data in {{vendor}} is current and complete (share classes, option pool, outstanding grants, recent transactions) — flag any gaps or stale entries you find rather than editing them yourself.
4. Fill in the 409A intake form fields: company details, valuation date, most recent financing terms, and any requested financial/operational inputs, using the information I've provided.
5. Select or confirm the refresh cadence if the platform supports scheduled updates.
6. Save the draft order in {{vendor}} without submitting or authorizing payment/engagement.

What done looks like: a fully filled-out, saved draft 409A order in {{vendor}} with the cap table data verified as current, ready for an authorized officer to review and submit.

Report back to me with: a summary of the fields you filled in, any cap table discrepancies or missing data you found, the draft's location/status in {{vendor}}, and a checklist confirming everything is ready. Then stop for human sign-off — an authorized officer must review and formally submit the engagement.

fund_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 409A valuation questionnaire that our valuation provider (e.g., Carta or similar) requires before they can produce the valuation report. Your job is to draft and pre-populate as much of the questionnaire as possible using our existing company records, then stop for my review.

First, ask me for anything you don't already have access to: our cap table export, latest financial statements (balance sheet, P&L, cash flow), most recent board deck or investor updates, details of any recent funding rounds or convertible notes, headcount and org changes since the last valuation, and any material business developments (new product launches, major contracts, pivots, litigation, etc.). Also ask which valuation provider's questionnaire we're completing and get me the actual form or portal link if you can access it.

Using these inputs, draft answers for all objective/factual sections: company overview, capitalization structure, financial history and projections, comparable company or transaction data if requested, and prior valuation details. Clearly flag any question requiring subjective business judgment (e.g., risk factors, strategic outlook, likelihood of exit scenarios, discount rate assumptions) with a placeholder noting 'FOUNDER INPUT NEEDED.'

Compile everything into a single organized draft (document or filled-in form fields) so I can review, correct, and add my own judgment answers efficiently. Do not submit the questionnaire or communicate with the valuation provider on my behalf — this remains a human step, and after preparing the draft you must stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the completed draft questionnaire, a list of flagged judgment-based questions needing my input, and any data gaps you found in our records that I need to fill before submission.

fund_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track a 409A valuation that I've already commissioned through {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform. The valuation firm typically takes 2-3 weeks to complete its independent analysis and return a report; that turnaround itself remains a human step and cannot be accelerated or performed by you.

What I need from you now is to prepare a monitoring routine and status summary so I know the moment the report is ready, without me having to manually check every day.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for my {{vendor}} issuer ID (or help me locate it in the {{vendor}} dashboard) if I haven't provided it, and confirm I have working configured credentials for {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard access.
2. Using the fair market values endpoint (GET /v1alpha1/issuers/{issuer_id}/fair_market_values) or the equivalent dashboard view, check whether a completed 409A valuation with fair market value data now exists for our issuer.
3. If no valuation is yet available, report back clearly that the report is still pending, note today's date, and calculate how many business days remain in the typical 2-3 week window based on when the valuation was ordered (ask me for that order date if you don't have it).
4. If a valuation IS available, retrieve and summarize the key output: the fair market value per share, the valuation date, and the expiration/refresh date, and flag it as ready for my review.
5. Set up a simple recurring check-in plan (e.g., "check again in 3-4 business days") and tell me what to do next each time — either "still waiting" or "valuation ready, review the numbers."

Done looks like: I have a clear, dated status report — either confirming the valuation is still in progress with an estimated completion window, or confirming it's complete with the fair market value data summarized — plus a simple plan for when to check again. Report back with this status and the polling plan.

fund_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me review a completed 409A valuation report before it is formally accepted by the company. Please do the preparatory work only — final acceptance must remain a human act.

First, ask me for: (1) the PDF/document of the 409A valuation report (from whichever independent valuation firm we used), (2) the date of the underlying valuation event and the intended 'as of' date, (3) our most recent cap table or option grant data, and (4) any prior 409A report for comparison, if one exists.

Once I provide these, please:
1. Summarize the report's key outputs: fair market value per common share, valuation methodology used, valuation date, and expiration/validity window (typically 12 months or until a material event).
2. Cross-check the FMV and share counts against our current cap table for consistency (e.g., matching share classes, total shares outstanding, recent grants).
3. Flag any material discrepancies, unusual assumptions, or changes versus the prior valuation (if supplied), such as large swings in FMV, methodology changes, or missing sections (e.g., no discount for lack of marketability explanation).
4. Draft a concise summary memo for the officer/board listing: the proposed FMV per share, valuation date, expiration date, and any flagged concerns, plus a suggested board resolution/consent language formally accepting the valuation for IRS safe-harbor purposes.
5. Prepare a checklist confirming: report received, cap table reconciled, no unresolved discrepancies, and memo/resolution ready for signature.

Do not accept, adopt, sign, or approve the valuation yourself, and do not instruct me to do so via automated action — this decision carries legal weight for IRS safe-harbor reliance and must be an officer's own authoritative act. When your review and drafts are complete, present the summary memo, checklist, and any flagged issues, and then stop for human sign-off.
